commands.result: FAIL reproduced; duplicate identity state is accepted in-process then rejected on restart, and a failed marker restoration opens the external literature writer

findings.title: OR-based persisted lookup can commit identity-drifting duplicate evidence
findings.detail: _persisted_observation_for_input selects candidates matching either observation_id or idempotency_key and then chooses by status and lexicographic observation_id. The two identities are not interchangeable: LiteratureBase rejects an observation_id reused for another logical source, and the state validator requires the persisted record selected for duplicate evidence to have the input idempotency key. _save_state authenticates the state but does not run the full state validator before committing it.
findings.reproduction: Persist observed OBS-A for URI /a and content a and OBS-B for URI /b and content b. First process OBS-B so its key is in seen_observation_keys, then submit an input with observation_id OBS-A but URI /b and content b. The seen-key path at lines 882-898 returns DUPLICATE with OBS-A because lines 1037-1057 select the ID match. The current process persists successfully. A new runner rejects the state with 'duplicate item evidence idempotency key conflicts' at lines 2321-2327. This is deterministic durable identity drift from valid SourceObservation input, not a stale-contract or acceptance-rebinding issue. The alternate persisted-ID tests cover a non-ambiguous key match and do not cover this cross-match.

findings.title: The commit can retire its only recovery journal before literature data is durable
findings.detail: ArtifactStore.put_bytes writes the blob and replaces it without fsyncing the blob or its containing directory, save_manifest does the same for manifest.json, and LiteratureBase._record does the same for observations.json at lines 411-417. TopicObservationRunner._save_state snapshots those files, writes and fsyncs the topic transaction/state/authentication/key files, verifies the in-memory snapshot, and then _remove_transaction retires and removes the journal at lines 2582-2591. A root-directory fsync for the topic files is not a durability barrier for the literature files or their nested directories.
findings.reproduction: Use the import path that writes an artifact and both literature manifests, then model power loss after the topic state, authentication, signing key, and COMMIT_INTENT/retirement directory entries are durable but before the literature blob/manifest file data and parent directories are durable. On restart the journal is gone, while the authenticated state names a literature snapshot whose files may be stale or missing; recovery has no target snapshot available and the literature/state binding fails or has already lost the imported data. The focused suite checks recovery deletion fsync calls and journal retirement, but injects no power-loss boundary around the import writes.

findings.title: Retiring-fence restoration can fail open
findings.detail: _remove_retired_transaction unlinks the retiring marker, fsyncs the topic root, and on fsync failure attempts to restore the marker. Restoration errors at lines 1623-1629 are swallowed before the method raises. The storage locks then unwind, and LiteratureBase._topic_transaction_pending sees no active or retiring marker, so an independent writer is allowed to mutate literature while the commit outcome remains unresolved.
findings.reproduction: In a temporary directory, inject an OSError for the root fsync after the retiring marker is unlinked and independently fail _atomic_write_bytes before it can restore that marker. The runner raises the expected durable-retirement error, but the marker is absent after lock release and a separate LiteratureBase.import_bytes returns IMPORTED. If the non-durable unlink later reappears after a crash, recovery can apply the transaction snapshot and discard that external import. test_retirement_fsync_failure_keeps_external_writer_fenced only exercises successful marker restoration.

findings.title: Regression tests do not exercise the blocking branches found above
findings.detail: The 66 focused tests pass, including the alternate persisted-ID replay test and the retirement-fsync test, but they do not combine an observation_id collision with a different persisted idempotency key, do not validate state before _save_state commits it, do not inject failure of retiring-marker restoration, and do not exercise literature blob/manifest fsync ordering through a crash boundary. Passing tests therefore do not establish the claimed identity and durability remediation.
findings.reproduction: The focused unittest command passes with zero skips. The missing cases are reachable by the mixed OBS-A/OBS-B duplicate sequence above and by the two-stage retirement fault injection above; neither sequence is present in the reviewed test files.
